title: Rice paper breakfast bagel
summary: A sheet of rice paper dipped in beaten egg, wrapped round scrambled egg and bacon and air fried into something that genuinely holds a bagel shape. About 21 g of protein, and no bread involved.

time.note: Makes one bagel. Scale it a sheet at a time.

nutrition_per_serving.note: One bagel. Two large eggs carry most of this on their own; medium eggs take about 20 calories off.

ingredients.note: This is the bagel. Nothing else here holds a shape.
Doing two jobs. The beaten egg is the soak that softens the sheet and then sets and browns it into a crust, and the rest is the filling. A flax egg does neither.
Leave it out and you have an egg and Parmesan bagel, which still works.

steps: Beat the eggs in a shallow bowl, wide enough to lay the rice paper sheet flat in.

Dip the rice paper into the beaten egg until it softens. The egg is doing the job water does for a spring roll wrapper, except it also sets and browns, which is what gives you a crust instead of a translucent sheet.
Scramble the rest of the egg in a pan with the bacon, then take it off the heat.
Pile the scrambled egg, bacon and Parmesan into the middle of the softened sheet.

Fold the sheet over the filling and shape it into a ring in your cupped hand, pushing a hole through the centre. It is slippery at this point, so keep the seam underneath and let it sit a moment to grip before you move it.
Air fry at 180C for 10 to 15 minutes, until golden and crisp.
tips: Do not leave the sheet in the egg. It goes from stiff to unmanageable in seconds, and an over-soaked sheet tears as soon as you try to fold it.
Make the hole bigger than you think. It closes up as the wrapper puffs and sets.
Let the scramble cool a little before it goes in, or the steam softens the wrapper from the inside and the seam opens in the basket.
It is at its best straight out of the air fryer. Left to sit, the filling steams the crust soft from within.
health_notes: The two eggs carry most of the 21 g of protein and nearly all of the 16 g of fat. The rice paper is the only real source of carbohydrate here and it weighs very little, which is the whole reason this comes in well under a bread bagel.

source.title: Air Fryer Rice Paper Bagels
source.adapted: Ingredients and method are as given in the video description, with the shaping detail taken from the video itself: the ring is formed by hand and the hole pushed through the middle. Nutrition is not recorded as stated. The description claims 214 calories, but two large eggs and 10 g of Parmesan come to about 199 on their own, which leaves roughly 15 calories for a rice paper sheet, 20 g of bacon and the sesame seeds. Recalculated at about 280.
